judges: DeepSeek V4 Pro, two blind runs, high effort
ruling: Doug, 2026-11-19: "I approve of the consolidation sheet as recommended with split decisions kept separate"

judge_a.why: Both use h6030 for the act of answering/responding: Job 9:3 'he could not answer Him' and Job 33:13 'He answers nothing a man asks.' The second adds no distinct sense.

judge_b.why: Both use h6030 in the literal sense of answering/responding: Job 9:3 'he could not answer Him' and Job 33:13 'He answers nothing a man asks' both refer to a verbal reply.

judge_a.why: Mark 1:22 uses g1849 of Jesus' teaching authority, whereas Titus 3:1 uses the plural for 'rulers and authorities' as governing powers; not the same sense.

judge_b.why: Mark 1:22 'taught as one who had authority' uses g1849 for the abstract quality/power of Jesus' teaching, whereas Titus 3:1 'submit to rulers and authorities' uses the plural for governing persons/office-holders; quality vs. persons is a different sense.

judge_a.why: They share the literal Hebrew servant/slave sense in Gen 9:25, but the second also contains 2Cor 4:5 'ourselves as your servants for Jesus' sake', a Greek figurative use not the h5650 literal slave sense of the first.

But the second also lists 2Cor 4:5 'ourselves as your servants for Jesus' sake,' a Greek figurative sense not h5650; if that verse belongs to the record it is different, so the record's data is unsettled.

judge_a.why: Both use h1926 as a noun for splendor/majesty: Job 31:26 'the moon moving in splendor' and Job 31:23 'His splendor I cannot overpower'; same sense, different bearer.

judge_b.why: Job 31:26 'the moon moving in splendor' and Job 31:23 'His splendor I cannot overpower' both use h1926 for the same noun sense of majestic splendor; the referent differs, not the word's job.

judge_a.why: Both use h1121 for literal offspring/sons: Gen 16:11 'bear a son' and Gen 4:25 'gave birth to a son'; singular versus plural is not a different sense.

judge_b.why: Both use h1121 for literal son/offspring: Gen 16:11 'you will bear a son' and Gen 4:25 'she gave birth to a son'; the singular/plural difference is only number, and the literal sense is already held in the first.

judge_a.why: Job 5:23 "you will have a covenant with the stones of the field" uses h1285 as a pact/agreement, matching the figurative covenant already in the first card at Job 31:1 "I have made a covenant with my eyes."

judge_b.why: Both records use h1285 for covenant/pact. The first already includes the figurative 'covenant with my eyes' (Job 31:1), so 'a covenant with the stones of the field' (Job 5:23) is the same sense, not a new one; the second even duplicates the Jonathan relation at 1Sa 18:3.

judge_a.why: The first card's verses use plural "days" for a human lifetime (Gen 6:3 "his days shall be 120 years"; Isa 53:10 "He will prolong His days"), whereas the second card's verses use singular "day" literally (Gen 1:5 "God called the light day... the first day").

judge_b.why: The first card uses h3117 for lifetime/duration: 'his days shall be 120 years' (Gen 6:3) and 'He will prolong His days' (Isa 53:10). The second uses it for literal calendar days/daylight: 'God called the light day... the first day' (Gen 1:5).

judge_a.why: The first card is God's transitive destroying/blotting out (Deut 6:15 "He will wipe you off the face of the earth"; Gen 6:7 "I will blot out man"), while the second card's verses are intransitive perishing (Job 3:3 "May the day of my birth perish"; Job 4:11 "The old lion perishes").

judge_b.why: The first card is destruction as calamity/judgment: 'He will wipe you off the face of the earth' (Deut 6:15) and 'You will laugh at destruction and famine' (Job 5:22). The second is ordinary perishing/dying: 'The old lion perishes for lack of prey' (Job 4:11) and 'By the breath of God they perish' (Job 4:9).

judge_a.why: The second's only verse, Job 8:13 "the hope of the godless will perish," is already attached to the first card as a speaks_of relation, and both use h6 in the intransitive "perish" sense.

judge_b.why: Both use h6 intransitively for perishing/coming to nothing. The first already has 'unnoticed, they perish forever' (Job 4:20) and even a relation to Bildad at Job 8:13, which is the second card's own verse.

judge_a.why: Both use h5172 for the same practice of divination: Joseph's cup "uses for divination" (Gen 44:5) and Laban "I have learned by divination" (Gen 30:27).

judge_b.why: Both use h5172 for divination as a means of obtaining hidden knowledge. Gen 44:5's cup 'uses for divination' and Gen 30:27's 'I have learned by divination' are the same sense, just different instances.

judge_a.why: Both use h241 for the literal ear as the organ of hearing: 'my ears caught a whisper' (Job 4:12) and 'opens their ears in oppression' (Job 36:15), where opening the ears is an idiom for causing to hear, not a different sense.

judge_b.why: Both records use h241 for the literal organ of hearing: Job 13:17 has 'let my declaration ring in your ears' and Job 36:15 has 'opens their ears in oppression'; singular versus plural does not change the sense.

judge_a.why: Both use h2758 for the same agricultural act of plowing: 'without plowing or harvesting' (Gen 45:6) and 'the oxen were plowing' (Job 1:14).

judge_b.why: Gen 45:6's 'without plowing or harvesting' and Job 1:14's 'while the oxen were plowing' both refer to the same agricultural activity of plowing the ground.

judge_a.why: Both use h3899 in the ordinary sense of physical food: 'good for food' (Gen 2:9) and 'I sigh when food is put before me' (Job 3:24).

judge_b.why: Gen 2:9's 'good for food,' Job 38:41's 'provides food for the raven,' and Job 3:24's 'when food is put before me' all use h3899 in the same literal sense of food/nourishment.

judge_a.why: Titus 2:10 uses pistis as 'faithfulness/fidelity' ('showing all good faith'), whereas the kept card has pistis as saving belief/trust in God ('justified through faith,' Rom 5:1; 'faith, hope, and love,' 1 Cor 13:13).

judge_a.why: Both use h4390 in the ordinary transitive sense 'to fill': 'fill the earth' (Gen 1:28) and 'filled their houses with silver' / 'fill your mouth with laughter' (Job 3:15; 8:21).

judge_a.why: Job 17:5's 'denounces his friends for a price' uses the same payment/bribe sense as the kept card's 'offer me a bribe from your wealth' (Job 6:22) and the Balaam wages relation at 2Pe 2:15.

judge_b.why: Both use g3408 in the same reward/payment sense: Gen 15:1 'your very great reward' and Job 6:22 'offer me a bribe from your wealth' already hold the sense, and Job 17:5 'for a price' uses it the same way.

judge_a.why: Gen 33:15's 'some of my people' is the same collective h5971 sense as the kept card's 'the rest of the people' (Gen 14:16) and 'you are the people' (Job 12:2): a group of people.

judge_b.why: Gen 33:15 'some of my people' is the ordinary collective/people-group sense of h5971 already present in Gen 14:16 'the rest of the people' and Job 12:2 'you are the people'; the possessive use adds no new sense.

judge_a.why: Gen 12:5's 'the people they had acquired' is the same collective human-group sense as the kept card's 'the rest of the people' (Gen 14:16), and both are Abraham taking people.

judge_b.why: Gen 12:5 'people they had acquired in Haran' denotes acquired household/servants, whereas the first card's sense is a people group/nation, as in Gen 14:16 'the rest of the people' and Job 12:2 'you are the people'.

judge_a.why: Both are literal agricultural furrows: 'hold him to the furrow' (Job 39:10) and 'its furrows weep' (Job 31:38); singular versus plural is not a different sense.

judge_b.why: Both are literal agricultural furrow(s): Job 39:10 'hold him to the furrow with a harness' and Job 31:38 'its furrows weep together' use h8525 in the same sense, singular versus plural only.

judge_a.why: Job 34:21's 'He sees his every step' uses the same figurative h6806 sense as the kept card's 'count my steps' (Job 14:16) and Job 31:37: human conduct observed by God.

judge_b.why: Both use h6806 for the steps of a person's life or conduct: Job 14:16 'You would count my steps' and Job 34:21 'He sees his every step' are the same figurative 'steps' sense, singular versus plural only.

judge_a.why: Gen 8:2 and Job 38:29 use h8064 for the sky/heavens from which rain and frost come, and Gen 1:8/14 use it for the expanse/sky where the lights are placed; the second card does not add a distinct sense beyond the first's 'sky over the earth.'

judge_b.why: Both records use h8064 for the sky/heavens above the earth: the first has "the floodgates of the heavens were closed" (Gen 8:2) and "the laws of the heavens" (Job 38:33), while the second's "God called the expanse 'sky'" (Gen 1:8) and "lights in the expanse of the sky" (Gen 1:14) are the same sense.

judge_a.why: Job 31:2 uses it for 'heritage from the Almighty' and Job 20:29 for 'the inheritance God has appointed him'; the first card already holds that divine-allotment sense, so the second verse would lose nothing.

judge_b.why: The second's only verse, "the inheritance God has appointed him" (Job 20:29), uses h5159 in the same God-appointed lot sense as the first already holds in "the heritage from the Almighty on high" (Job 31:2).

judge_a.why: Isa 53:9 'He had done no violence' and Job 16:17 'my hands are free of violence' use the same moral-wrongdoing sense as Gen 6:11's 'full of violence.'

judge_b.why: Job 16:17, "my hands are free of violence," uses h2555 in the same wrongdoing/innocence sense as Isa 53:9, "He had done no violence," and Gen 6:11, "full of violence."

judge_a.why: Gen 21:23 'the same kindness that I have shown to you' already holds the human covenant kindness/loyalty sense of Job 6:14 'the kindness of his friend.'

judge_b.why: Job 6:14, "A despairing man should have the kindness of his friend," uses h2617 for human loyal kindness, the same sense the first already holds in Gen 21:23: "Show to me... the same kindness that I have shown to you."

judge_a.why: Prov 8:15 'By me kings reign' already holds the human ruler sense of Job 12:18 'He loosens the bonds placed by kings.'

judge_b.why: The second's "He loosens the bonds placed by kings" (Job 12:18) uses h4428 for human rulers, the same sense as the first's plural verse "By me kings reign" (Prov 8:15).

judge_a.why: Same household female servant/slave: Gen 32:22 'his two maidservants' and Gen 16:1 'an Egyptian maidservant named Hagar' both use h8198 for a household maidservant; Gen 12:16 and Gen 20:14 likewise list acquired maidservants.

judge_b.why: Both cards use h8198 for a female household servant/maidservant: Gen 32:22 ('his two maidservants') and Gen 16:1-3 (Hagar as Sarai's Egyptian maidservant) are the same role, singular versus plural only.

judge_a.why: Same sense of spoken word(s)/speech: Deut 6:6 'these words I am commanding' and Prov 2:1 'my words' already hold the content of speech, while Gen 30:34 'as you have said' and Gen 44:18 'speak a word' are the singular of that same spoken-word idea.

judge_b.why: Both cards use h1697 for speech/words: Deut 6:6 ('these words'), Prov 2:1 ('my words'), and Gen 30:34 ('let it be as you have said') are all the same sense of spoken or commanded words, not different ideas.

judge_a.why: Both are the same rare term h108 for mist/vapor: Job 36:27 'rain from the mist' and Gen 2:6 (h108, rendered 'springs' in English) denote the vapor/water-source rising and watering; the English word is not a separate Hebrew sense.

judge_b.why: Both use h108 for mist/vapor rising from the earth/water: Job 36:27 ('distill the rain from the mist') and Gen 2:6 (the mist/springs watering the ground) are the same thing, not two senses.

judge_a.why: Same literal bodily nakedness: Job 24:7 'Without clothing, they spend the night naked' and Job 22:6/24:10, like Gen 3:10-11 in the first card ('I was afraid because I was naked'), use h6174 for lacking clothing.

judge_b.why: Both use h6174 for literal nakedness without clothing: Job 1:21 ('naked I came... and naked I will return') and Job 24:7 ('they spend the night naked') are the same condition, not figurative versus literal.

judge_a.why: Same people-group/nation sense: Gen 10:32 'nations of the earth' and Job 12:23 'He makes nations great' already hold h1471 for peoples; Gen 17:20 'a great nation' and Job 34:29 'man and nation' are the singular of the same idea.

judge_b.why: Both use h1471 for a people/nation: Gen 10:31-32 ('their... nations') and Gen 17:20 ('a great nation') are the same sense, singular versus plural only.

judge_a.why: Gen 24:21 and Job 15:21 in the first card already cover the state of a person's God-given success/prosperity, and Job 30:15 uses the same state: 'my prosperity has passed like a cloud.'

judge_b.why: Both use h8001 for a person's state of well-being/prosperity: "in his prosperity" (Job 15:21) and "my prosperity has passed" (Job 30:15); Gen 24:21's "success" is the same favorable outcome.

judge_a.why: The first card already has divine punishment/calamity for sin: 'My punishment is greater than I can bear' (Gen 4:13) and calamity for 'the workers of iniquity' (Job 31:3); the second is the same retribution, 'wrath brings punishment by the sword' (Job 19:29).

judge_a.why: Both are the literal created sea(s). The first already has the sea as God shut it in ('Who enclosed the sea behind doors', Job 38:8), and Gen 1:10 uses the plural for the same created waters: 'the gathering of waters He called seas.'

judge_b.why: Both refer to the same literal body of water, only singular vs plural: "waves of the sea" (Job 9:8) and "the gathering of waters He called seas" (Gen 1:10).

judge_a.why: Both use the word for a visible God-given sign that indicates something: the rainbow is 'the sign of the covenant' (Gen 9:12), and the lights are 'signs to mark the seasons and days and years' (Gen 1:14).

judge_b.why: Both are visible tokens appointed by God as signs: "This is the sign of the covenant" (Gen 9:12) and "let them be signs to mark the seasons..." (Gen 1:14).

judge_a.why: Both use h6662 as a substantive for righteous people as a class: Ps 34:17 'The righteous cry out, and the LORD hears' and Job 27:17 'the righteous will wear' do the same job, so one card loses nothing.

judge_b.why: Job 27:17 'what he lays up, the righteous will wear' uses h6662 for the righteous as a class of people, the same sense as Ps 34:15 'the eyes of the LORD are on the righteous'; singular/plural is only a number difference.

judge_a.why: Both use h490 for the same class of women whose husbands are dead: Gen 38:11 'Live as a widow...' and Job 22:9 'You sent widows away empty-handed' are the same sense, differing only in singular versus plural.

judge_b.why: Job 22:9 'You sent widows away empty-handed' uses h490 in the same literal sense of women whose husbands have died as Gen 38:11 'Live as a widow' and Job 24:3 'the widow's ox.'

judge_a.why: Both use h8141 for a year/years as a unit of time: Gen 1:14 '...seasons and days and years' and Job 3:6 '...the days of the year' are the same sense, differing only in singular versus plural.
